Subject: Private offer request — ACME/Redwood (rev-share + term ask)

Stephanie — thanks again for the demo last week. ACME is ready to move forward but we need two concessions on the AWS Private Offer to get procurement to sign: (1) reduce marketplace rev-share to 10% (our legal team pushed back on the standard 20%), and (2) a 24-month committed term with a 30-day termination clause tied to annual usage thresholds.

I've attached a short term sheet and our SOW. If Redwood can accept the 10% rev-share and the 24-month term, we can expedite to our procurement and legal and sign the private offer within 7–10 days. If not, please advise the best counter.

Happy to jump on a call today if helpful.

Subject: RE: Private offer request — ACME/Redwood (rev-share + term ask)

Jordan / Vivek — looping you in on ACME's private-offer asks. Key points: they want rev-share at 10% (vs our standard marketplace 20%) and a 24-month committed term with an early termination window (30 days) tied to usage thresholds. They indicated speed to signature if we accept.

Why this is non-standard: 10% rev-share materially lowers our expected marketplace take and 24-months with an early out reduces revenue certainty. Customer lifetime is attractive (we estimate $1.2M ARR on the table), and they're a referenceable retail brand which helps in vertical GTM.

What I need from deal desk / execs for an approval path:
- Exec-level exception to marketplace rev-share (approve 10% or counter)
- Guidance on term length (24 months ask) and whether we can accept an early termination tied to usage (or require 6 months notice)
- Any required commercial concessions (credits, onboarding, marketing) to trade for the rev-share reduction

I've attached the term sheet they sent. Jordan — can you run a quick ARR model and propose a recommended counter (target rev-share and term)? Vivek — can you indicate whether exec deviation is available for strategic references?

If helpful, I'm available for a 30-min sync at 11:30 PT.

Attachments: ACME_Private_Offer_Request_20270309.pdf, Redwood_Term_Sheet_v1.3.pdf

—Stephanie Nguyen

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private offer request — ACME/Redwood (rev-share + term ask)

Thanks Steph — I ran the quick numbers. Assumptions based on their projections and ACME's usage profile:
- ARR estimate: ~$1.2M over first 12 months if adoption is as expected
- Marketplace take @20% (standard) -> Redwood net ~$960k (after rev-share? typo: compute properly)
- Marketplace take @10% -> Redwood net uplift of ~120k in the first year vs 20% baseline (model attached)

My recommendation for a pragmatic counter that balances revenue and go-to-market value:
- Rev-share: 12.5% (split the delta)
- Term: 18 months (not 24) with an opt-out after 12 months with 60 days notice (no early termination for convenience in first 12 months)
- Require ACME to commit to a short joint case study + marketplace promotional tile (marketing requirement)

We will need executive sign-off for any rev-share below 15% and for term >12 months. Vivek — can you weigh in on whether this is approvable as an exec exception (they are strategic and referenceable, but we shouldn't set a precedent). Also looping Lisa (AWS) to ensure the proposed rev-share and marketing commitments align with AWS marketplace rules for private offers.

Steph / Jordan — after reviewing the ask and the recommended counter, I'm willing to provide an executive exception with conditions. Approvals below are conditional on legal and finance accepting the related protections:

Approved exceptions (conditional):
- Rev-share: Approve special rev-share at 12.5% (one-time exec exception)
- Term: Approve 18-month term with the following constraints: no termination for convenience in first 12 months; after 12 months, ACME may terminate with 60 days notice if usage < agreed threshold

Conditions to sign:
1) Legal (internal + AWS marketplace legal) must sign off on contract language and marketplace mechanics (Lisa, please confirm AWS side).
2) Customer must agree to a Redwood case study + marketplace feature (marketing collateral) within 90 days of go-live; failure to deliver reverts rev-share to standard 20% for the remainder of the term.
3) Finance to confirm revenue recognition and billing flows for the private offer; require HubSpot deal record RDW-2027-ACME-57 and signed SOW on file.
4) Executive approval is a one-off and not precedent — include language that this rate is specific to ACME deal id RDW-2027-ACME-57.

Jordan — please prepare an approval memo (1 page) summarizing ARR impact, comps to similar exceptions, and the proposed contract language for legal to review. Steph — please confirm ACME is okay with the marketing requirement before we route legal.
